MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 14, 2021

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN at 7:04 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Flag salute led by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton
  Associate Planner Kelley Thom

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  RECOGNITION OF ASSOCIATE PLANNER KELLEY THOM'S RETIREMENT

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN recognized Associate Planner Kelley Thom in her many
accomplishments while working for the City of Rolling Hills Estates for the last fifteen years.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, TO
  APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-F AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF SEPTEMBER 2021

  APPROVED WARRANTS 64257 THROUGH 64302 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $153,866.48 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 090121 THROUGH
  090221; 64190V; IN THE AMOUNT OF $79,020.92 FOR A GRAND TOTAL
  AMOUNT OF $232,887.40 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF AUGUST 24, 2021

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
SEPTEMBER 14, 2021
 D.  TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF AUGUST 17, 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF AUGUST 23, 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION BY FS CONTRACTORS INC. FOR THE JOHN AND
  LYNN TABER GROVE PROJECT

  FOUND TABER GROVE PROJECT COMPLETE WITH FS CONSTRUCTION
  INC. IN THE GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $58,400 AND DIRECTED THE
  CITY CLERK TO RECORD A NOTICE OF COMPLETION (ATTACHED)
  WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY RECORDER’S OFFICE, HOLDING A
  5% RETENTION PAYMENT OF $2,920 FOR 35-DAYS FROM RECORDING.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

NONE.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  APPEAL OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION’S DECISION TO APPROVE PLANNING
  APPLICATION NO. 210244 AT 2 BRANDING IRON LANE

Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

There being no objection, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

Appellant representative William Beverly spoke on behalf of Nancy McDonough, summarizing
the basis of the appeal of the Planning Commission’s decision, specifically as it relates to the
existence and maintenance of the bridle trail on the property. He explained that the appellant
is requesting the Council confirm the continuing validity and efficacy of the bridle trail
conditions, and require continued compliance as a material part of any approval of the current
project.

Mr. Beverly read aloud the email sent on behalf of Ms. McDonough to the Council as part of
the record this afternoon, as requested by City Attorney Davis, summarizing the history of the
usage of the bridle trail.

Applicants Joe and Sapna Dangaran spoke, requesting that the Council approve the Planning
Commission application with the conditions of approval related to the bridle trail under dispute
so they may proceed with their building permit application. They then summarized the
information they uncovered during their due diligence they performed when purchasing and
also while planning the building of the new home.

The Dangarans stated that they were not planning to keep horses on their property, in response
to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

MAYOR PRE TEM ZERUNYAN welcomed the Dangaran family to the City of Rolling Hills
Estates. He recommended upholding the original condition creating the lot split, while
approving the current plans for the home.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF to:

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
SEPTEMBER 14, 2021
   APPROVE THE BUILDING PLANS AND UPHOLD THE APPEAL ON THE
  BASIS OF THE EXISTENCE OF THE CONDITION THAT WAS THERE
  WHEN THE LOTS WERE CREATED.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ also welcomed the Dangarans to the City.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba explained that in a 2018 planning
application on this property, the trail was to remain in the proposed improvements within the
plan so this issue did not come up, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ agreed that the documentation before the Council clearly
states the intended use for the bridle trail, and stated she supports the motion of MAYOR
PRO TEM ZERUNYAN.

City Attorney Davis noted that although the dedication required was not recorded, as a
matter of law, the law recognizes implied dedications. In this case, the fencing and historic
use of the trail, which does not need to be continuous, has created an implied dedication
which is sufficient under the law.

Discussion ensued regarding whether or not to allow the applicants to proceed with the
building application, or if it should be re-reviewed by the Planning Commission with changes
made to the bridle trail portion of the plans.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA noted that she supports the motion, and confirmed with the
City Attorney that a Resolution to enforce the condition can be brought back to the Council at
the next City Council meeting on September 28.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN amended his motion, seconded by COUNCIL
  MEMBER STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL
  CALL VOTE:

  AFFIRM THE PLANNING COMMISSION’S DECISION TO APPROVE PA-
  210244 AS CONDITIONED; AND UPHOLD THE APPEAL ON THE BASIS OF
  THE EXISTENCE AND ACCEPTANCE OF PRIOR CONDITIONS OF
  APPROVAL RELATED TO THE LOT SPLIT CREATING THE PARCEL THAT
  REQUIRED THE CONSTRUCTION AND MAINTENANCE OF A BRIDLE
  TRAIL, WITH SUCH DETERMINATION TO BE BROUGHT BACK TO THE
  COUNCIL IN THE FORM OF A RESOLUTION.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  FIRST AMENDMENT TO CITY MANAGER EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT

City Attorney Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN confirmed there were no other changes to the employment agreement.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ commended City Manager Grammer for his work as City
Manager during her year as Mayor and through the pandemic.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No additional public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE FIRST AMENDMENT TO THE CITY MANAGER
  EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT AND AUTHORIZE ITS EXECUTION BY THE
  MAYOR.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
SEPTEMBER 14, 2021
   AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM: 3717 PALOS VERDES DRIVE
  NORTH - ADDRESS NUMBER SIGN

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA stated she supports the addition of the signs, particularly to
assist emergency services in locating these houses.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF agreed with COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA, noting that this has
been a confusing location for a long time.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN agreed with both Council Members, and noted that this confusion often
leads to many unnecessary U-turns for drivers missing their correct turn.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE FOLLOWING: 1) RE-FACE THE EXISTING DOBBIN LANE
  WHITE FREE-STANDING SIGN LOCATED IN THE PUBLIC RIGHT-OF-WAY,
  ON THE SOUTH SIDE OF PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH, FOR
  EASTBOUND TRAFFIC, TO INDICATE THE ADDRESSES OF 3717, 3719,
  AND 3721 PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH; 2) INSTALL THE SAME SIGN
  PLACARD ON THE BACK OF THE EXISTING DOBBIN LANE SIGN FOR THE
  SAME THREE ADDRESSES FOR WESTBOUND TRAFFIC ON PALOS
  VERDES DRIVE NORTH; AND 3) INSTALL A NEW SIGN CLOSER TO
  DOBBIN LANE, FURTHER EAST OF 3717 PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH,
  ALSO ON THE SOUTH SIDE OF PVDN, IN A LOCATION TO BE
  DETERMINED BY STAFF, FOR DIRECTING EASTBOUND TRAFFIC TO
  DOBBIN LANE.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

C.  TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM: MASONGATE DRIVE -
  EQUESTRIAN CROSSWALK

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material).

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba stated that one of the Traffic &
Safety Committee Members brought this item to the Committee for their consideration, in
response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA noted that the trail near the Pepper Tree is below grade,
making visibility very limited from the road as riders and runners come up from the trail
towards the street. She also noted her concerns about enforcement after the striping is done,
and stated she would like to see the Pepper Tree preserved and trimmed to improve
visibility.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA also noted the new striping may prevent people from
parking and blocking the horse trail.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted he also supports pruning and preserving the Pepper
Tree.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
SEPTEMBER 14, 2021
 Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPROVE THE FOLLOWING EQUESTRIAN IMPROVEMENTS ON
  MASONGATE DRIVE: 1) ADD STRIPING FOR AN EQUESTRIAN
  CROSSWALK; 2) ADD A NEW “TRAIL CROSSING” SIGN AT THE LOCATION
  OF THE EXISTING BIKE SIGN; 3) MOVE THE EXISTING BIKE SIGN CLOSER
  TO THE EXISTING CROSSWALK; 4) TRIM AND MAINTAIN THE PEPPER
  TREE ON THE EAST SIDE OF THE STREET ADJACENT TO THE BRIDLE
  TRAIL AND CLEAR THE BRUSH ON THE OPPOSITE SIDE OF THE STREET;
  5) INVESTIGATE THE REMOVAL OF THE CONCRETE CURBS ON EACH
  SIDE OF THE STREET FOR BETTER BRIDLE TRAIL ACCESS SUBJECT TO
  PROPER DRAINAGE AND COSTS.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER AND STATUS OF
  CITY EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

City Manager Grammer reported that the current Los Angeles County Health Officer Order is
still in effect requiring masks for all indoor public settings, regardless of vaccination status.
Hospitalization rates and infection rates across the County have been dropping. There have
been 30 new COVID cases in RHE since the last City Council meeting on August 24.
Vaccination rates continue to be very high in RHE, with 85.3% of people 12 and older having
received at least one dose of the vaccine, 98% of those ages 12-17, and over 98% of those 65
and older.

The annual City Celebration will be held outdoors on Saturday, September 25 at the Empty
Saddle Club. Additionally, the Prepared Peninsula Expo will be held on October 24 at
Peninsula High School adjacent to the farmer’s market, and the Tracy Austin Doubles
Tournament has been confirmed for November 12 – 14.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported that a meeting of the Palos Verdes Peninsula Chamber
of Commerce Legislative Committee was held earlier today, where they announced that the
Annual Legislative Forum will be held virtually this year on October 15 from 12:00 pm – 2:00
pm.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also attended the Taber Grove project dedication ceremony,
officially opening the pocket park donated by the Taber family.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also reported that the South Bay Cities Council of Government
(SBCCOG) Steering Committee voted to send a letter to the Governor asking him to sign AB
361 extending the emergency waiver of the Brown Act allowing for the continuation of virtual
public meeting which is set to expire September 30. The SBCCOG has also been encouraging
the opposition of the Governor signing SB 9 and SB 10 related to the affordable housing crisis,
which would greatly impact local control and zoning.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN attended the Strategic Development session as an Executive
Board Member of the California Contract Cities Association (CCCA), where safety
requirements for the upcoming CCCA Fall Education Summit were discussed.
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
SEPTEMBER 14, 2021
 MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN also reported that he will be attending the Southern California
Association of Governments (SCAG) Community, Economic & Human Development
Committee and Emerging Technologies Committee meetings virtually this coming week.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

NONE.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2)
  Significant Exposure to litigation: two potential cases

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION.

B.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATORS
  Government Code Section 54956.8
  Property: Fee interest in property on Palos Verdes Drive East between Palos Verdes
  Drive North and Harbor Sight Drive
  Agency negotiator: City Manager, Community Development & Public Works Director,

  Negotiating parties: Metropolitan Water District
  Under negotiation: price and terms of payment

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:52 P.M. MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN adjourned the City Council meeting in honor
of Dale Allen. The meeting was adjourned to the next regular City Council meeting on
Tuesday, September 28, 2021 at 7:00 pm for the purpose of a Regular meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Steve Zuckerman
City Clerk  Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
SEPTEMBER 14, 2021
